reviewStatus.notes: Starting rule set for medical review. Every rule below must be reviewed and signed off by a qualified medical professional before clinical deployment. Rules deliberately over-trigger (conservative bias): false positives redirect users to care, false negatives endanger them.

low.message: Your symptoms appear manageable at home for now, but monitor them closely and consult a doctor if they worsen.

medium.message: Your symptoms may benefit from medical attention. Consider booking an appointment in the near future.

high.message: Your symptoms may require prompt medical attention.

emergency.message: Your symptoms suggest a possible medical emergency. Seek immediate professional medical attention.

emergencyRules.rationale: Could indicate a cardiac event. Must never be substituted with self-care advice.
Could indicate respiratory or cardiac compromise.
Loss of consciousness is an acute emergency.
Syncope can indicate cardiac or neurological emergencies.
Active or recent seizure requires emergency evaluation.
Sudden weakness or paralysis is a stroke signal.
High fever can accompany serious infection. Threshold values intentionally left to medical review.
Upper GI bleeding requires prompt evaluation.
Speech difficulty can be a stroke signal.
Mental health emergency. User should be directed to immediate support, not self-care.

highRules.rationale: Severe abdominal pain may require prompt evaluation.
New leg swelling can indicate vascular issues.
Sudden visual changes can indicate serious conditions.
Inability to keep fluids down risks dehydration.
